newsitem.title: USA: Folgers raises coffee prices -- again.
newsitem.headline: Folgers raises coffee prices -- again.

text.p: Folgers Coffee Co. said Monday it was raising coffee prices -- again.
The company, the largest roaster in the United States, said it was raising the price of 13-ounce cans of regular and decaffeinated ground coffee by 30 cents to $3.36 and $4.06.
That leaves Folgers' prices almost 50 percent higher than they were before the Procter & Gamble Co. unit started raising prices in February. Folgers' prices are often matched by competitors.
"The price of Folgers coffee generally reflects the price of green coffee sold on the commodity market," Folgers said in a statement.

It said green coffee prices have been rising since January because of lower crop estimates for the upcoming harvest in Brazil, the world's biggest producer. It also cited reduced stocks of coffee from other major producers such as Colombia and countries in Central America, and generally tight supplies of high quality arabica beans on worldwide markets.
Folgers raised the price of its 13-ounce can of coffee on Feb. 11, March 10 and April 29. On Feb. 20, it said it was boosting the increase it had announced on Feb. 11.
The increases, including Monday's 30-cent hike, which takes effect immediately, amount to $1.10, or almost 49 percent on the regular 13-ounce can.
The company also raised the price of Folgers Instant Coffee by 1.25 cents an ounce, taking the list price up to $3.96 for the 8-ounce size. The price for single serving packets will remain unchanged.
